hints: Look at what the IR peaks are telling you about functional groups, especially the peak at 1720 and the missing peak above 3100.
A strong absorption around 1720 cm-1 means a C=O group is present, while no broad peak above 3100 cm-1 rules out an O-H group.
Check which of the three named structures contain C=O but no O-H, and see why only the two esters fit the formula and spectrum.
walkthrough:
**Decode the IR spectrum**

Think of IR as a fingerprint for bonds. A strong peak is telling you that bond is definitely there.

Key IR correlations:
$$\text{C=O stretch} \approx 1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$
$$\text{C-O stretch} \approx 1000-1300 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$
$$\text{O-H (alcohol, acid) stretch} \approx 3200-3600 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$

**Apply to molecule X**

X has a strong peak at 1720 cm-1, so it contains C=O. It has a strong peak at 1250 cm-1, so it contains C-O. It has no strong peak above 3100 cm-1, so it has no O-H group.

That combination of C=O plus C-O with no O-H points strongly to an ester, $\text{RCOOR'}$.

**Test statements 1, 2 and 3**

1 ethyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is an ester with formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$. It has C=O and C-O but no O-H, so it fits perfectly.

2 methyl butanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$, is an isomeric ester, also $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$. It also has C=O and C-O but no O-H, so it fits perfectly.

3 1-hydroxypentan-3-one, $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, has formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$ and has C=O, but it also has an alcohol O-H. That would give a broad strong peak above 3100 cm-1, which is absent. So 3 is ruled out.

**Conclude the combination**

Only 1 and 2 are possible. 3 is impossible.

That corresponds to 1 and 2 only are correct.

options.A: This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 is wrong because 1-hydroxypentan-3-one contains an alcohol O-H group which would show a broad strong absorption above 3100 cm-1.
options.B: This option states 1 and 2 only are correct. Both ethyl propanoate and methyl butanoate are esters with formula C5H10O2, giving C=O at 1720 cm-1 and C-O at 1250 cm-1 with no O-H peak above 3100 cm-1. Statement 3 is correctly excluded.
options.C: This option claims 2 and 3 only are correct. Statement 2 is correct, but statement 3 is incorrect due to its O-H group, and statement 1 is incorrectly left out even though ethyl propanoate fits the data just as well as methyl butanoate.
options.D: This option claims 1 only is correct. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is also correct because methyl butanoate is simply a structural isomer of ethyl propanoate with the same functional groups and same IR pattern.
